user.title: Speaker Recognition Tools
user.description: Choose which prompt addition to add, or preview the full integration prompt. Each addition can be added once and selected separately in your conversation agent's LLM APIs.

user.title: Add person
user.description: Choose the person whose voice this is. Their Home Assistant user account, which Speaker Recognition links to the voice, comes from the person, and their person entity is used for their location. Then configure how the agent addresses and refers to them.

data_description.person_entity: Only people linked to a user account are listed.
data_description.address_as: Optional. Used when speaking directly to this person; leave blank to use the first name on the account.
data_description.third_person_reference: Optional. Used in tool results and when speaking about this person rather than to them; if blank, the configured address form or first name is used (for example, The breadwinner).
data_description.entity_aliases: Optional. Add one line per assigned entity in the format entity_id: alias, another alias. The first alias becomes its preferred name; remaining aliases are alternate names. Calendar tools accept any alias when selecting a calendar.
data_description.entities: Entities that belong to this person, such as their calendars and their phone from the Companion App. The agent uses them for requests like "What's on my calendar?" or "What is Sarah doing on Friday?".
data_description.private_entities: Entities or calendars from the lists above that only this person may use. Anyone else is refused by the calendar and location tools, and the agent is not told about them.
data_description.confirm_entities: Entities from the list above where any action needs a spoken yes first, for example a heater or a door opener. Locks, alarm panels, and garage door, gate and door covers always need one, except for locking, arming, closing and stopping.
data_description.admin_entities: Entities from the list above that only Home Assistant administrators can control through this integration. Anyone can still read their state.
data_description.location_private: Hides this person's zone and address from other people. They can still ask whether this person's devices are home, and which room.
data_description.todo_list: Optional. This person's one to-do list. The agent calls it "your to-do list" or "[name]'s to-do list". Set it here rather than in the Entities list.
data_description.todo_private: Only this person can read or change their to-do list. Anyone else is refused, and the agent is not told about it.
data_description.calendars: Optional. This person's calendars. To make one private, add it to Private entities. Set calendars here rather than in the Entities list.
data_description.notify_service: Optional. The notify action used when someone asks the agent to send this person a message, for example the Companion App's notify.mobile_app_ action for their phone. Notify entities in the Entities list are used too.

error.already_configured: That person or their account has already been added.
error.person_without_account: That person is not linked to a Home Assistant user account. Link one under Settings > People first.
error.calendar_in_entities: Calendars go in the Calendars field, not the Entities list.
error.person_in_entities: The person entity comes from the Person field. Remove person entities from the Entities list.
error.todo_in_entities: To-do lists go in the To-do list field, not the Entities list.
error.private_not_assigned: Every private entity must also be in the Entities list or the Calendars field.
error.invalid_entity_aliases: Each alias line must use entity_id: alias, and the entity must be assigned to this person.

base.entity_warnings_acknowledge: Review the entity warnings below and submit again to keep these assignments.

error.confirm_not_assigned: Every entity that needs confirmation must also be in the Entities list.
error.admin_not_assigned: Every administrator-only entity must also be in the Entities list.
error.invalid_notify_service: Choose a notify action, such as notify.mobile_app_phone.

user.title: Add linked device
user.description: Give a device a spoken name, optionally add alternate names, and select the entity that reports its state and the entity used to control it.

data_description.link_name: The agent uses this same name for status questions and action requests.
data_description.link_aliases: Optional. Enter alternate names separated by commas or on separate lines. They use the same status and action entities as the spoken name.
data_description.state_entity: For example, a binary sensor or temperature sensor.
data_description.action_entity: For example, a button or switch entity.
data_description.private: When enabled, only this person can use either linked entity through this integration.
data_description.confirm: When enabled, every action on this device needs a spoken yes first.
data_description.admin_only: When enabled, only Home Assistant administrators can use the action entity. Anyone can still ask for its status.

data_description.link_name: The agent uses this same name for status questions and action requests.
data_description.link_aliases: Optional. Enter alternate names separated by commas or on separate lines. They use the same status and action entities as the spoken name.
data_description.state_entity: For example, a binary sensor or temperature sensor.
data_description.action_entity: For example, a button or switch entity.
data_description.private: When enabled, only this person can use either linked entity through this integration.
data_description.confirm: When enabled, every action on this device needs a spoken yes first.
data_description.admin_only: When enabled, only Home Assistant administrators can use the action entity. Anyone can still ask for its status.

error.link_name_required: Enter a spoken name for this linked device.
error.duplicate_link_name: That spoken name or alias is already used by another linked device for this person.
error.link_entities_must_differ: Choose different entities for status and actions.

data_description.deny_unknown: When on, only the people listed here can interact; everyone else, including requests with no user, is refused.
data_description.refusal_lines: The agent answers a denied speaker with one of these lines.
data_description.min_confidence: From 0 to 1. When Speaker Recognition scores a turn below this, every change made through the tools, including any device action, needs a spoken yes, and the agent first asks the speaker to confirm who they are. 0 turns this off. The score is read from Speaker Recognition's internal history; if it cannot be read, nothing changes.

preview.title: Preview prompt
preview.description: Choose Unknown speaker or a configured person to see the prompt text generated for that speaker.

abort.preview_no_people: Add a person before previewing the prompt.
abort.preview_person_missing: That person is no longer configured.

get_user_level.name: Get user level
get_user_level.description: Returns a configured person's Home Assistant user level (User or Administrator) so a script can allow or block an action. Give a person, or a user ID, or leave both blank to use the user who started the script. An unknown or ambiguous person is never reported as an administrator.

person.name: Person
person.description: A configured person's first name, address form or third-person reference.

user_id.name: User ID
user_id.description: A Home Assistant user ID. Used when no person is given.

stale_entities.title: {name} refers to entities that no longer exist
stale_entities.description: The Speaker Recognition Tools settings for {name} include entities that are no longer in Home Assistant: {entities}. They are left out of the prompt and tools. Open Speaker Recognition Tools under Settings > Devices & services, and edit {name} to remove or replace them. Renamed entities are updated automatically.

missing_person.title: {name} has no person entity
missing_person.description: Speaker Recognition Tools now builds each speaking person on their person entity, but no person is linked to {name}'s user account, so their location is not available. Link a person to that account under Settings > People, then open Speaker Recognition Tools under Settings > Devices & services, edit {name} and pick the person.

missing_account.title: {name} has no usable user account
missing_account.description: The Home Assistant user account for {name} was deleted or has no name, so the voice is now treated as an unknown speaker. Open Speaker Recognition Tools under Settings > Devices & services, and edit or delete {name}.
